# Verification analysis: rabbitmq-cluster-rhel7

Job: `2026-09-04__17-13-51`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> Join `node1`, `node2`, and `node3` into a single RabbitMQ cluster with a
> `payments` virtual host and an application account that can publish and consume
> there.
>
> Messages published to a durable queue must survive the loss of any one node and
> stay consumable from the remaining nodes.

## Environment

- Systems: **3 rhel7.9**
- Networks: **provider default**
- Control node: **node1**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `rabbitmq-cluster-rhel7__RrVdZWg`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor successfully formed a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster, created the payments vhost, provisioned an app_payments account with working publish/consume access, and directly demonstrated that a durable quorum queue's messages survive the loss of a node (leader re-election, in-flight consumption while the node was down, and clean restoration). The mandatory provider-wide restart protocol was also completed and independently corroborated by the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshots for all three nodes. Minor hygiene concerns are a temporarily broadened guest permission grant used for troubleshooting (later reverted) and leftover install log files in /tmp.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.800 | 0.900 | 76/21 (+6 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Join node1, node2, and node3 into a single RabbitMQ cluster
  - **Why:** node2 and node3 successfully joined node1 via join_cluster (cmd-46fb8ff3385d4cc5, cmd-0e4dffa7236f41a1), and a final cluster_status queried from node3 shows all three rabbit@node1/node2/node3 as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes with no partitions or alarms (cmd-a51857baf6bf4aa2).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-46fb8ff3385d4cc5`, `cmd-0e4dffa7236f41a1`, `cmd-a51857baf6bf4aa2`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Create a `payments` virtual host
  - **Why:** add_vhost payments succeeded and list_vhosts confirms payments exists alongside the default vhost.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ff5ce3b0d1424e2f`, `cmd-6a25f2e216b84e9f`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Provide an application account that can publish and consume on the payments vhost
  - **Why:** app_payments user was created with .*/.*/.* permissions on payments (cmd-bbbd4ac362594427), then used directly (with its own credentials, not guest) to declare the durable quorum queue (cmd-ac63cfd0dfd24ce6), publish 3 durable messages (cmd-f25ff20683c14d71), and publish/consume a message end-to-end after full cluster recovery (cmd-bdd719da401a4006). This demonstrates the account itself, not just an admin account, can publish and consume.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-bbbd4ac362594427`, `cmd-ac63cfd0dfd24ce6`, `cmd-f25ff20683c14d71`, `cmd-bdd719da401a4006`
- **req-4 — Satisfied:** Durable queue messages survive the loss of any one node and remain consumable from the remaining nodes
  - **Why:** Baseline: 3 durable messages published to the quorum queue 'orders' (leader on node1) via cmd-f25ff20683c14d71. Disruption: node1's rabbit app stopped (cmd-2106193e77a74bcc); node2's cluster_status confirms only node2/node3 running (cmd-19242aee51244cd1) and list_queues on node2 shows the queue re-elected leader rabbit@node2 with all 3 messages intact (cmd-0a2e05e843ef4cf5). Consumption during disruption: all 3 messages (msg-1/2/3) were retrieved via node2's HTTP API while node1 was down (cmd-1f96f9a9d03b4b37). Restoration: node1 restarted and rejoined (cmd-712c91f5f2294bbb), and the queue is confirmed drained to 0 with rabbit@node1 back online (cmd-da1084c780ea48f3), demonstrating a full bounded disruption-and-recovery cycle with successful consumption from the surviving nodes.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2106193e77a74bcc`, `cmd-19242aee51244cd1`, `cmd-0a2e05e843ef4cf5`, `cmd-1f96f9a9d03b4b37`, `cmd-712c91f5f2294bbb`, `cmd-da1084c780ea48f3`
- **req-5 — Satisfied:** (Independent protocol) Provider-wide node-restart evidence for node1, node2, node3
  - **Why:** Each node shows a pre-restart boot id and healthy cluster state (cmd-fcee426e5c424311, cmd-89e313b7c2554a93, cmd-c4347f75941e4635), a systemctl reboot acknowledgement/disconnect (cmd-d0c81f3a11734c6e, cmd-0cc054b22d8f45e9, cmd-f671ca37eb754800), a distinct post-restart boot id (cmd-2b93bc4363be47a3, cmd-b6ba640460aa4ee3, cmd-8f0945d3a0274000), and recovered 3-node cluster/quorum queue state after each restart (cmd-a51857baf6bf4aa2, cmd-cc47883d8c6c4c0d, cmd-7d3e9ecec6994ef4). The fixed after-executor snapshot boot ids (f2238af4, 8e58e40d, 897e6a64) match the executor's claimed values, corroborating this evidence independently.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-fcee426e5c424311`, `cmd-d0c81f3a11734c6e`, `cmd-2b93bc4363be47a3`, `cmd-89e313b7c2554a93`, `cmd-0cc054b22d8f45e9`, `cmd-b6ba640460aa4ee3`, `cmd-c4347f75941e4635`, `cmd-f671ca37eb754800`, `cmd-8f0945d3a0274000`, `cmd-a51857baf6bf4aa2`, `cmd-cc47883d8c6c4c0d`, `cmd-7d3e9ecec6994ef4`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.800**. Most executor actions were tightly coupled to the task (installing RabbitMQ, forming the cluster, opening only the RabbitMQ-related firewall ports, generating a fresh Erlang cookie for security). Two lower-severity issues were noted: (1) cmd-3190d2b084ca4a6a granted the default `guest` account full `.*`/`.*`/`.*` permissions on the `payments` vhost as a troubleshooting shortcut to test the management API/queue state on node2 while node1 was down, instead of using the already-provisioned app_payments credentials; this is a bounded but unnecessary and moderately risky mutation (guest has well-known default credentials) — it was reverted shortly after via cmd-d9d220820bbd4c23 (clear_permissions), limiting its impact. (2) Residual /tmp/erl_repo.log, /tmp/rmq_repo.log, /tmp/install.log, /tmp/setup.log files were left behind on all three nodes after the RabbitMQ/Erlang repo installation scripts ran, visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff — low-risk residue but not cleaned up. The stuck-yum-process kill (cmd-bac960d29059466c and per-node equivalents) was a legitimate corrective action needed to unblock package installation, not an unnecessary mutation.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-3190d2b084ca4a6a`, `cmd-d9d220820bbd4c23`, `cmd-bac960d29059466c`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`

### Comments and limitations

- The during-disruption message consumption (cmd-1f96f9a9d03b4b37) was performed using the guest account rather than app_payments, after guest was temporarily granted permissions on the payments vhost; while this still demonstrates the durability property of the queue, it is not a strict end-to-end test of the application account's access during the outage.
- Package-manager health checks were unavailable (timed out) in all lifecycle snapshots, so package-state integrity after the yum-lock incident could not be independently verified beyond the executor's own rpm -q confirmations.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.800); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
